title: basics / GitHub Copilot in the terminal
content: ## GitHub Copilot in the terminal If you have access to [GitHub Copilot](/docs/setup/copilot.md), you can use it to get AI-powered help with terminal commands and shell scripting. There are several ways to use Copilot with the terminal: ### Terminal inline chat Start an inline chat directly in the terminal to get help with shell commands: 1. Open the terminal (`kb(workbench.action.terminal.toggleTerminal)`) 2. Press `kb(workbench.action.terminal.chat.start)` or run the **Terminal Inline Chat** command from the Command Palette 3. Enter your question or request in natural language, such as: * "How do I find the largest files in this directory?" * "Show me how to undo the last git commit" * "Create a bash script to analyze log files" ![Terminal inline chat helps you quickly get and run shell commands](./images/basics/terminal-chat-2.png) When Copilot provides a response, you can select **Run** to execute the command directly or **Insert** to add it to the terminal for further editing. For more information about using GitHub Copilot with the terminal, see [Use terminal inline chat](/docs/chat/inline-chat.md#use-terminal-inline-chat). ### Ask about terminal commands Ask the agent directly about shell commands and attach relevant terminal output. For example, ask `How do I search for a pattern recursively?` or `Explain this command without running it`. The `@terminal` chat participant is deprecated and is not supported in the Copilot harness. See [Replace chat participants](/docs/agent-customization/migrate-customizations.md#replace-chat-participants). ### Reference terminal context in chat You can include terminal information as context in your chat prompts: * Use `#terminalSelection` to add selected text from the terminal to your chat prompt * Use `#terminalLastCommand` to include the last command you ran in the terminal
